findings.body:
Replacing `json.loads` with `pickle.loads` on untrusted session data creates a remote code execution vector. An attacker who can supply the `raw` value can craft a pickle payload that executes arbitrary code on the next `load_session` call.

```suggestion
    return json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(raw))
```

Use a safe format (JSON) or a restricted unpickler with an allow-list of permitted classes.

summary: The change replaces JSON session decoding with pickle. This introduces a critical remote-code-execution surface because `load_session` now deserializes attacker-controlled bytes with `pickle.loads`.

verification.reason: The change replaces json.loads with pickle.loads on base64-decoded session input (web/session.py), which is a classic arbitrary-code-execution vector on untrusted data. Base revision used safe JSON; the regression and critical severity are both supported.
